question: Which of the following is the last five year plan of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __the__ __**Twelfth.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Twelfth Five-Year Plan (2012–2017) was the last officially implemented Five-Year Plan in India.
 
• After this, the planning process was discontinued, and the NITI Aayog was established in 2015 to replace the Planning Commission,
 
 
• shifting focus to a long-term development strategy rather than fixed-term plans.
 
 
 
• The Twelfth Plan aimed to promote inclusive growth, ensuring that the benefits of economic growth reached all sections of society, especially marginalized groups.
 
• The plan emphasized sustainable development, focusing on environmental sustainability and reducing the carbon footprint of economic activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 2015, the Planning Commission was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** (National Institution for Transforming India), which shifted the focus from fixed-term planning to a more flexible approach to policy-making and governance.
 
• The NITI Aayog emphasizes long-term vision and strategy, moving away from the traditional Five-Year Plans.
 
• Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997–2002)
 
 
• The Ninth Plan prioritized human development, aiming to improve the quality of life through initiatives in health, education, and employment.
 
• It recognized the importance of investing in human capital to drive economic growth.
 
• A key objective was to reduce poverty and enhance social justice.
 
• The plan introduced various poverty alleviation programs and targeted interventions to uplift marginalized sections of society, with a goal to reduce the poverty ratio significantly.
 
 
 
• Tenth Five-Year Plan (2002–2007)
 
 
• The Tenth Plan aimed for a GDP growth rate of 8% per annum, emphasizing job creation and improving the employment situation in India. It recognized the need for inclusive growth to ensure that the benefits of economic development reached all sectors of society.
 
• This plan also focused on enhancing infrastructure, particularly in rural areas, to facilitate economic activities. Investments were directed towards transportation, power, and irrigation, crucial for agricultural productivity and overall economic growth.
 
 
 
• Eleventh Five-Year Plan (2007–2012)
 
 
• The Eleventh Plan aimed for a GDP growth rate of 9% per annum, focusing on creating jobs and reducing poverty.
 
• It sought to build a competitive and sustainable economy by promoting innovation and entrepreneurship.
 
• It emphasized social inclusion, targeting the needs of disadvantaged groups.
 
• The plan aimed to enhance access to quality education, health services, and basic amenities, ensuring that development was equitable and inclusive.
